approach: Extend the gate's attribution walk with a mode (incremental or full replay). Incremental picks the newest checkpoint by records-branch commit order, then judges only first-parent main commits after its main_sha. It lists records added since its records_sha with diff-tree --diff-filter=A and parses only those. For each new landing it resolves the cited intent by id or path with a single blob read, and it audits only the records commits in records_sha..tip. Incremental falls back to a full replay, with the reason reported as replay_reason (not a finding), when the check version differs, main_sha is off main, or records_sha is not an ancestor of the tip. Full replay ignores checkpoints for trust, loads and audits everything, then compares with the newest checkpoint and adds a CheckpointDisagrees finding naming the checkpoint when a commit at or before its main_sha has a finding or main_sha is not on main. Every report carries seconds, commits judged and records judged, in text and JSON. A checkpoint is written only after a clean pass, from local runs, and after a landing. CI passes --read-only. An ignored fixture test with about 200 landings gives the CHANGELOG timings.

decisions.choice: Newest checkpoint is chosen by records-branch commit order: walk the records first-parent log from the tip and take the first commit that added a checkpoints/<id>.json. created_at is never used for ordering. Document this in code and in the design doc.
decisions.reason: created_at is self-reported (history.rs), so a forged later timestamp could otherwise win. Branch order is set by the audited history.

rejected.why: Ids are not guaranteed to be ordered.

decisions.choice: Incremental work is bounded by what is new. It audits records history only for records_sha..tip. It parses only records added since records_sha. For each new landing it resolves the cited intent via the intent id/path and reads that one blob. It does not call read_records over the whole tree. records_judged counts the added records. The fixture test asserts that the number of blobs parsed (a counter in the reader) equals added records plus cited older intents.
decisions.reason: The design doc (section 9) requires incremental time not to scale with old records. Counting alone, as in the previous plan, did not deliver that.

rejected.option: Read all records and count only new ones

rejected.why: Same scaling problem. Full replay keeps the full audit.

decisions.choice: A non-ancestor records_sha, a different version, or a main_sha off main in an incremental run is reported as replay_reason with effective mode FullReplay. CheckpointDisagrees is raised only by a full replay (requested, or forced after fallback) when the comparison fails. A forced replay due to a non-ancestor records_sha still compares with the checkpoint, so the disagreement is reported once, from the replay comparison, and the reason says why the replay ran.
decisions.reason: Separates the fallback trigger from the finding. A checkpoint with a bad records_sha is a tampered record and the replay should name it. This avoids the double report the critic flagged.

rejected.option: Emit CheckpointDisagrees at the incremental fallback

decisions.choice: The checkpoint names the last passing main commit before the first pending commit. It is written only when the report has no findings.
decisions.reason: A pending commit's 15-minute window can still expire into a finding. A checkpoint past it would hide that finding from later incremental runs.

rejected.option: Checkpoint at the main tip even with pending commits
rejected.why: An expired pending commit would never be judged again.

decisions.choice: Check version is a constant ATTRIBUTION_CHECK_VERSION in attribution.rs, stored in Checkpoint.verifier_version. A mismatch forces a full replay with the reason reported.
decisions.reason: Only a rule change makes past passes untrustworthy.

decisions.choice: An explicit --read-only flag, also implied by the CI env var. CI passes the flag and keeps permissions contents: read. Binary tests that expect a write call env_remove("CI"). Tests of the read-only behavior set CI=true explicitly, or pass the flag.
decisions.reason: Code-enforced no-write mode backed by workflow permission. cargo test runs under CI=true in GitHub Actions, so write tests must not inherit it.

rejected.why: Not enforced in the local path.

decisions.choice: The land checkpoint is written from the CLI Land command after land_pr returns Landed with a merged_commit. gh.rs is untouched.
decisions.reason: gh.rs is not a deliverable. The landing record is already written first by land_pr.

rejected.option: Add a method to LandingRecords in gh.rs

files.purpose: Mode enum, ATTRIBUTION_CHECK_VERSION, checkpoint reader that picks the newest by records-branch order, bounded incremental reader (added records plus cited intents), range audit, fallback reasons, full-replay comparison with CheckpointDisagrees, report fields, write_checkpoint, tests including the ignored fixture_timings.
Re-export the new API; keep legacy wrappers compiling.
CHECKPOINT_DIR constant and Checkpoint path/constructor helper; record type unchanged.
--full-replay and --read-only flags, CI-env rule, write on pass, post-landing checkpoint helper, Check doc comment.
Text and JSON show mode, reason, seconds, commits and records judged; label the new finding kind.
Help, JSON keys, exit code on a tampered checkpoint, read-only/CI writes nothing; write tests env_remove CI.
Attribution job: incremental read-only on push, read-only full replay on schedule; permissions unchanged.
Entry with measured-on-fixture timings and a note that the real-repo timing follows landing.
Record job-6 decisions in sections 9 and 10, including checkpoint ordering and bounded incremental reads.

steps: history.rs: add CHECKPOINT_DIR and a path helper, with a small test.
attribution.rs: add Mode, ATTRIBUTION_CHECK_VERSION, the new report fields, and FindingKind::CheckpointDisagrees with its label.
attribution.rs: list checkpoints and pick the newest by records-branch first-parent order, not created_at; add a test with a forged created_at.
attribution.rs: decide incremental vs forced replay (version, main_sha off main, records_sha not an ancestor) and record replay_reason.

attribution.rs: in incremental mode, list added records via diff-tree --diff-filter=A, parse only those, resolve cited older intents by path, audit only records_sha..tip, and count parsed blobs for the test.
attribution.rs: start the main walk after the checkpoint main_sha and time the run with Instant.

attribution.rs: in full replay, load and audit everything, compare with the newest checkpoint, and add CheckpointDisagrees; compute checkpoint_main before the first pending commit; add write_checkpoint, acting only on a clean report.
attribution.rs tests: incremental, tampered, version change, non-ancestor records_sha, write/no-write, pending, ignored fixture_timings.
main.rs: flags, CI-env rule, write on pass, post-landing helper with a unit test, doc comment.
display.rs: text and JSON output with unit tests.
binary.rs: help, JSON and exit-code tests, env_remove("CI") on write tests.
ci.yml: split the attribution step by event and add --read-only.
Run cargo fmt, clippy and test; run the ignored fixture test; put the printed numbers in CHANGELOG; update docs/design/records-history.md.

risks.risk: A ~200-landing fixture makes the timing test slow.
risks.mitigation: Write the records in one RecordsWriter::append with many Changes; mark the test #[ignore].

risks.risk: Changing the walk's signature breaks check_attribution_with_legacy and its tests.
risks.mitigation: Keep check_attribution's signature as a full-replay wrapper; add the mode function beside it.

risks.risk: A tampered checkpoint with a non-ancestor records_sha could crash the diff.
risks.mitigation: Check ancestry first. Report it as replay_reason and run the full replay; only the replay comparison raises CheckpointDisagrees.

risks.risk: Resolving a cited intent by id/path may miss intents stored under a different layout, which would wrongly report a landing as missing.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the same path scheme as read_records; if a lookup misses, fall back to a full replay with a reason rather than raising a finding.

risks.risk: Binary write tests flake under CI=true in GitHub Actions.
risks.mitigation: Every write-expecting test calls env_remove("CI"); read-only tests set it explicitly.

risks.risk: CHANGELOG timings are invented or stale.
risks.mitigation: Run the ignored test, copy the printed values, and label them measured-on-fixture.

demonstrations.method: Gate test: build N attributed commits, run incremental (writes a checkpoint), add 2 attributed commits, run incrementally. Assert checked==2 and records_judged equals the added intents plus landings. Assert that a FullReplay run has checked==N+2. In the same test, assert the reader's parsed-blob counter equals the added records plus the older intents they cite, and is below the total record count.
demonstrations.observes: The incremental judged count equals the new commits, is less than the full replay's, and old records are not parsed.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without checkpoint reading, the incremental run judges N+2 commits and the equality assertion fails. Without bounded reading, the parsed counter equals the total.

demonstrations.method: Gate test: write a checkpoint naming an unattributed main commit with a valid records_sha. Incremental passes (it starts after that commit). FullReplay fails with Unattributed plus a CheckpointDisagrees finding whose detail contains the checkpoint id. A binary test runs check --attribution --full-replay and expects exit code 2.
demonstrations.observes: The replay reports a finding naming the checkpoint and fails.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the replay trusted the checkpoint it would skip those commits, pass, and the disagreement assertion would fail.

demonstrations.method: Gate test: a valid checkpoint with verifier_version 'attribution/0' naming a recent commit. Run incremental. Assert effective mode FullReplay, replay_reason mentions the version, and checked equals the total commit count. Add a test where records_sha is not an ancestor: assert replay_reason says so and the CheckpointDisagrees finding comes from the replay comparison.
demonstrations.observes: A version mismatch forces a full replay that judges everything.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the version comparison only commits after the checkpoint are judged and checked is too small.

demonstrations.method: Gate and CLI tests compare the records tip before and after. (a) A passing check writes one checkpoint with main sha, records tip and version. (b) A failing check leaves the tip unchanged. (c) --read-only and CI=true leave the tip unchanged on the same repo that writes without them; the write-expecting binary tests call env_remove("CI"). (d) The post-landing helper puts a checkpoint after the landing record. (e) A pending commit makes the checkpoint stop before it. (f) The newest checkpoint is chosen by branch order: a forged later created_at on an older checkpoint does not win.
demonstrations.observes: The tip moves only in the writing cases.
demonstrations.fails_without: If read-only did not suppress writes the tip would move in (c). If failing runs wrote, it would move in (b).

demonstrations.method: Run clippy over the workspace, then cargo fmt --check.
demonstrations.observes: Clippy exits 0 with no warnings, and the format check exits 0 with no diff.
demonstrations.fails_without: Any warning or unformatted code makes the command report it and exit non-zero.

demonstrations.method: Binary test asserts the help text contains --full-replay, --read-only, 'incremental' and no-write wording. Also read the output directly.
demonstrations.observes: Help documents incremental mode, --full-replay, and that --read-only and CI never write checkpoints.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the doc comment and new args the contains assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Display unit tests assert the text has 'second', 'commit(s) judged' and 'record(s) judged', and the JSON has numeric seconds, commits_judged and records_judged. A binary test parses check --attribution --json.
demonstrations.observes: Every run reports seconds, commits and records.
demonstrations.fails_without: The summary-line and JSON-key assertions fail if the fields are missing.

demonstrations.observes: Top-level permissions: contents: read unchanged. One --read-only step on push, and one --read-only --full-replay step with if github.event_name == 'schedule'. No step writes or pushes a checkpoint.

demonstrations.method: Run the ignored fixture test: about 200 landings, a full replay, then add one landing and checkpoint, then an incremental run one behind. Copy the printed seconds into the CHANGELOG, labeled measured-on-fixture, and state that the real-repository timing is taken after landing. Check them with git diff CHANGELOG.md.
demonstrations.observes: The printed full-replay and incremental seconds match the CHANGELOG. Incremental is lower and judges 1 commit.

demonstrations.method: The tamper test asserts the full replay judged commits at or before the checkpoint, and that the finding label and detail name the checkpoint id. A second test shows an unknown main_sha yields CheckpointDisagrees in a full replay.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the checkpoint were trusted in full replay, checked would be smaller than the total and no CheckpointDisagrees finding would appear.

open_questions: Which remote do local checkpoints get pushed to? The producer should find the remote GitLandingRecords::for_remote uses before choosing append vs append_to_remote.
Does records_branch::audit_history accept a commit range? If not, the producer adds a range variant in attribution.rs that runs the same checks over records_sha..tip. I did not read it in this round.
Is a local full-replay pass allowed to write a checkpoint? The plan allows it unless read-only.
